html:
A Javanese prince who led the Java War of 1825 to 1830 against Dutch rule. He is now a national hero of Indonesia.

He was the eldest son of the third sultan of Yogyakarta but was passed over for the throne. He lived outside the palace at Tegalrejo, studied Islam and had visions that he saw as a calling. Anger was high in Java over taxes, tolls, land leases and Dutch meddling at court. In 1825 the Dutch marked out a road across his land, and the clash that followed began the Java War.

Diponegoro called it a holy war and many Javanese saw him as the just king of prophecy. His forces fought a guerrilla war across central Java for five years. Some 200,000 Javanese died, mostly from hunger and disease. In 1830 the Dutch general Hendrik Merkus de Kock invited him to talks at Magelang and arrested him there. He was exiled to Manado and then to Fort Rotterdam in Makassar, where he died in 1855. The war left the Dutch in debt, and they soon brought in the Cultivation System to make Java pay. The painter Raden Saleh painted his arrest.
